heading: Article 265: Can Government Levy Taxes Without a Law?
tldr: Article 265 of the Indian Constitution mandates that no tax can be imposed or collected by the government without a valid law.
This constitutional provision acts as a fundamental safeguard against arbitrary taxation by any government authority.
Every tax, whether by the Central or State government, must be backed by legislation passed by Parliament or a State Legislature.
It ensures that citizens are protected from taxes that are not duly approved through the democratic legislative process.
Understanding Article 265 empowers taxpayers to question any tax demand lacking proper legal backing.
caption:
Ever wondered if the government can just make you pay a new tax whenever it wants? 🤔 The answer is a clear NO. India's Constitution says every single tax – big or small, central or state – must first become a proper law. This protects you from unfair taxes and ensures everything is approved democratically.
